title: Hard Lessons for Europe From the Ceuta Crisis
content: European Union leaders should have received several messages during the recent surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In particular, cohesion without trust is fragile; dependence without limits leads to vulnerability; and selective enforcement of international law risks eroding a pillar of Europe’s strategic identity.

title: The World’s Silent Majority for International Cooperation
content: The hollowing out of global institutions has resulted in a rapid loss of credibility for the international rule of law. But a majority of people worldwide still recognize the value of multilateralism, which countries can preserve in the absence of superpower consent by finding better ways to cooperate.

Reducing that dependence will require building industries that can compete globally while removing the structural barriers that prevent innovative Canadian firms from scaling.

For developing and developed economies alike, the timing could not be better.

But while investors have few alternatives, the bond-salesman-in-chief cannot be complacent.

But he must abandon his predecessor’s defensive approach.
